newsitem.title: UK: TREG says will not extend KEPIT bid.
newsitem.headline: TREG says will not extend KEPIT bid.

text.p: TR European Growth Trust (TREG) said on Friday that it will not extend its hostile bid for the 500 million pound Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust (KEPIT) beyond today's closing.

"The TREG Offers have focused a great deal of attention upon the question of poor performing investment trusts, the obligations of their Boards and investment managers and the right of shareholders to expect a full cash exit if the investment rationale at launch has not been fulfilled," Sir Geoffrey Littler, chairman of TR European Growth said.
"The Board of TR European Growth announces that it will not be extending its offers for KEPIT beyond today's closing date," TREG said.
"Our offers have resulted in the KEPIT Board putting forward proposals under which they estimate that KEPIT investors may receive a full cash exit of up to 532 million ponds," TREG's Littler addedd.

KEPIT -- which is offering investors the chance to invest in a continuing European privatisation unit trust, a general Europe unit trust managed by M&G or a cash exit via a Kleinwort Benson money market fund -- said on September 30 that its offer to shareholders was worth 106.4 pence per share, should they choose the money market fund option.

A bitter battle over the corpse of the investment trust, set up in 1994 in the expectation that the rest of Europe would generate the huge returns for shareholders that Britain did in the 1980s, erupted when TR European announced a hostile bid in July this year.
However, the battle appeared to have come to an end on Friday. -- David Chance London Newsroom 44 171 542 5887
